title: National Immunization Schedule
definition: MoHFW UIP schedule for universal infant immunization.
keyPoints: Birth: BCG, OPV-0, Hep-B birth dose
6 wk: OPV-1, Penta-1 (DPT+HepB+Hib), Rota-1, fIPV-1, PCV-1
14 wk: OPV-3, Penta-3, Rota-3, fIPV-2, PCV-2
16-24 mo: DPT booster, OPV booster, MR-2, JE-2, PCV booster
pearls: Total doses by 1 year: BCG+4 OPV+3 penta+3 rota+2 fIPV+2 PCV+1 MR.
clinicalContext: Nurse preparing 6-wk vaccination visit.
nursingPriority: Administer OPV-1 (2 drops oral), Penta-1 (0.5 mL IM anterolateral thigh), Rota-1, fIPV-1, PCV-1; record in MCP card.

title: Cold chain
definition: System of transporting/storing vaccines at prescribed temperature.
keyPoints: Deep freezer (-15 to -25°C): OPV, measles, MR for long-term
Do NOT freeze DPT, TT, HepB, Penta — freezing denatures
VVM (vaccine vial monitor): discard if stage 3 or 4
Shake test: check for freeze damage in DPT
pearls: Top shelf of ILR: OPV, measles; bottom: DPT, TT, HepB.
clinicalContext: ANM at outreach session has vaccine carrier.
nursingPriority: Keep carrier closed; place vaccines above ice packs; use within 4 h; check VVM and discard if square darker than circle.

title: Family planning methods
keyPoints: Barrier: condom (dual protection HIV+pregnancy), diaphragm, female condom
IUD: Cu-T 380A (10 y), 375 (5 y), LNG-IUS (5 y)
Hormonal: COC, POP, DMPA injection (q3 mo), implant (Nexplanon 3 y)
Emergency: LNG 1.5 mg <72 h, Cu-T <5 d
LAM: exclusive breastfeeding + amenorrhea + <6 mo (98% effective)
clinicalContext: 28-y-old P2 wants 5-year reversible method.
nursingPriority: Counsel Cu-T 380A (10 y) or LNG-IUS (5 y); rule out pregnancy, insert within 7 d of menses, teach thread check, 6-week follow-up.

title: Diarrhea and ORS management
keyPoints: Classify: no dehydration, some dehydration, severe
Plan A (no dehydration): home ORS + zinc
Plan B (some): ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 h
Plan C (severe): IV RL — 100 mL/kg: <12 mo 30 mL/kg in 1 h + 70 in 5 h; >=12 mo 30 in 30 min + 70 in 2.5 h
Zinc: 10 mg/d <6 mo, 20 mg/d >=6 mo x14 d
clinicalContext: 10-kg 14-mo-old with lethargy, sunken eyes, skin pinch goes back slowly, unable to drink.
nursingPriority: Severe dehydration — Plan C: IV RL 30 mL/kg (300 mL) in 30 min, then 70 mL/kg (700 mL) over 2.5 h; reassess q15-30 min; start ORS once able to drink.

title: Child growth and ICDS
keyPoints: Launched 1975; target: 0-6 y children, pregnant women, lactating mothers, adolescent girls
Services: supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-up, referral, pre-school education, nutrition and health education
Supplementary nutrition: 500 kcal/12-15 g protein for normal 6-36 mo; 800/20-25 for SAM
WHO growth chart — plot weight-for-age monthly
clinicalContext: AWW notes 2-y-old weight below -3Z on growth chart.
nursingPriority: Classify as SAM, refer to NRC, double ration supplementary nutrition, counsel mother on IYCF, deworm if not done.

topic: Nutritional guidelines for pregnant and lactating females
title: Nutritional guidelines for pregnant and lactating females
keyPoints: Lactation: +600 kcal first 6 mo, +520 after; +25 g protein
IFA: 60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid daily (pregnancy from 2nd trimester, continue 6 mo postpartum)
clinicalContext: Lactating mother at 3 mo postpartum.
nursingPriority: Recommend +600 kcal, +25 g protein, IFA + calcium + iodine, adequate fluids, diverse diet.

topic: Mosquito, ticks, mites, louse — identification and prevention
title: Mosquito, ticks, mites, louse — identification and prevention
keyPoints: Anopheles: malaria — breeds in clean water, female bites night
Aedes aegypti: dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever — daytime biter, stagnant clean water (coolers, tyres)
clinicalContext: Aedes containment in dengue outbreak.
nursingPriority: Source reduction — empty coolers weekly, cover water storage, use larvicide (temephos), long sleeves, repellents, fogging for adult vectors.

title: NTEP, NACP, NLEP
definition: National TB, HIV, and Leprosy programmes.
keyPoints: NTEP (formerly RNTCP): DBT under Nikshay Poshan Yojana 500 INR/mo; new drug regimen 2023 daily FDC
NACP V (2022-26): 95-95-95 targets; ART lifelong free
NLEP: MDT free; leprosy elimination <1/10,000 population; renewed focus on case detection 2023
clinicalContext: Sputum AFB+ patient under NTEP.
nursingPriority: Register in Nikshay, daily FDC 4-drug intensive 2 mo + 2-drug continuation 4 mo, monthly follow-up, Nikshay Poshan Yojana benefit, contact screening.

title: Malaria and vector-borne diseases
keyPoints: Malaria: P. vivax, P. falciparum (severe), P. malariae, P. ovale, P. knowlesi
Treatment: Pf — ACT (artesunate + sulfa-pyrimethamine); Pv — chloroquine + primaquine 14 d (radical cure)
clinicalContext: Child from endemic area with fever, P falciparum+ on RDT, GCS 10.
nursingPriority: Admit, start IV artesunate 2.4 mg/kg at 0/12/24 h then daily, supportive care, blood sugar, avoid steroids; notify NVBDCP.

title: Rickettsial disease
keyPoints: Scrub typhus (O. tsutsugamushi): chigger, eschar, rash, lymphadenopathy
Treatment: doxycycline 100 mg BD x7 d (first-line, all ages in India per AIIMS/ICMR)
clinicalContext: Child from hilly area with fever, eschar on thigh.
nursingPriority: Start doxycycline empirically; notify; supportive care; Weil-Felix positive to OX-K in scrub typhus.

title: Epidemiology and study design
definition: Study designs and measures of association.
keyPoints: Descriptive: case report, case series, cross-sectional
Case-control: look back; good for rare diseases
Incidence = new cases / population at risk; Prevalence = total cases / population
Relative risk = CI exposed / CI unexposed
clinicalContext: Study of 1000 smokers and 1000 non-smokers followed 10 y for lung cancer.
nursingPriority: Design is cohort; calculate relative risk as CI exposed / CI unexposed.

title: Mission Indradhanush
definition: MoHFW 2014 campaign to reach fully immunized status >90%.
keyPoints: Target: children <2 y and pregnant women partially or unimmunized
Full immunization coverage rose from 65% to >85% per NFHS-5
clinicalContext: AWW identifies 14 unimmunized children in village.
nursingPriority: Conduct MI session — OPV, BCG, Penta etc as per schedule, counsel parents, plan catch-up, Nikshay/UWin record.

title: National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)
definition: Launched 2005, part of National Health Mission now.
keyPoints: Goal: accessible, affordable, quality healthcare to rural poor
Key interventions: ASHA, JSY, ANMs upgrade, facility upgrade (SC, PHC, CHC, DH)
Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) for facilities
clinicalContext: PHC under NRHM.
nursingPriority: Follow IPHS norms — 30-bed PHC covers 30,000 plains / 20,000 hilly population, 1 medical officer.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
definition: Cash incentive for institutional delivery under NHM.
keyPoints: LPS states: 1400 rural, 1000 urban for mother; 600 rural, 200 urban for ASHA
HPS states: BPL/SC/ST only: 700 rural, 600 urban; 200 ASHA
Linked with JSSK for free entitlements
clinicalContext: ASHA escorts BPL pregnant woman to PHC in UP (LPS state).
nursingPriority: Register under JSY, ensure 2 ANC visits, institutional delivery, PNC; mother receives 1400 INR, ASHA 600 INR.

title: Disease determinants
keyPoints: Agent: biological, physical, chemical, nutritional, mechanical
Host: age, sex, genetics, immunity, nutrition
clinicalContext: Epidemic analysis.
nursingPriority: Identify agent-host-environment triad to plan intervention at weakest link.

title: Pathogenicity vs virulence
keyPoints: Pathogenicity: proportion of infected who become ill (secondary attack rate)
Virulence: proportion of ill who become severe/die (case fatality rate)
Infectivity: proportion exposed who become infected
clinicalContext: 100 exposed, 50 infected, 30 ill, 3 die.
nursingPriority: Infectivity 50%, pathogenicity 60%, virulence 10% (CFR).

title: Incubation period table
clinicalContext: Child develops fever + rash 12 d after exposure.
nursingPriority: Suspect measles (incubation 10-14 d); isolate with airborne precautions, notify surveillance.

title: Ascariasis
keyPoints: Loeffler syndrome: eosinophilic pneumonitis from larval migration
Treatment: albendazole 400 mg single dose (>2 y) or mebendazole 100 mg BD x3 d
clinicalContext: Child from rural area passing worms in stool.
nursingPriority: Give albendazole 400 mg single dose, treat family, improve sanitation, repeat deworming q6 mo.

title: Chickenpox
keyPoints: Incubation 14-21 d; infective 1-2 d before rash till all lesions crusted
Treatment: acyclovir for adults/immunocompromised; VZIG for exposure
clinicalContext: Child with fever and vesicular rash starting on trunk.
nursingPriority: Airborne + contact precautions, cool baths, calamine, avoid aspirin, acyclovir if severe/adult.

title: Measles
keyPoints: Rash: day 4 — maculopapular behind ears spreads caudally
Complications: pneumonia, diarrhea, encephalitis, SSPE, blindness
Vit A 2 doses on day 1 and 2 for all children with measles
clinicalContext: Unimmunized 2-y-old with fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots.
nursingPriority: Airborne isolation, vit A 100,000 IU day 1 and 2 (up to 200,000 IU in >=12 mo), supportive care, notify IDSP, catch-up MR.

title: Airborne, droplet, contact precautions
keyPoints: Airborne: TB, measles, varicella — N95, negative pressure room
Droplet: meningococcus, flu, pertussis, mumps, rubella — surgical mask, single room or cohort
Contact: MRSA, VRE, C. difficile, RSV — gown + gloves, dedicated equipment
clinicalContext: Sputum AFB+ TB patient.
nursingPriority: Airborne precautions — N95 respirator fit-tested, negative-pressure room, keep door closed, instruct cough etiquette.

title: Bordetella pertussis (whooping cough)
keyPoints: Stages: catarrhal (most infective) → paroxysmal (whoop + post-tussive vomit) → convalescent
clinicalContext: Infant with paroxysmal cough, whoop, cyanosis on cough.
nursingPriority: Droplet isolation, azithromycin 10 mg/kg x5 d, oxygen PRN, gentle feeding, treat household contacts.

title: Smallpox eradication
keyPoints: India declared free 1977; global eradication 1980 WHO
Strategies: surveillance + ring vaccination, freeze-dried vaccine
clinicalContext: Test item.
nursingPriority: Identify smallpox as the only human disease eradicated by immunization.

title: Hepatitis C and E
keyPoints: HCV (RNA, Flaviviridae): parenteral, sexual, perinatal; chronic in 70-80%; DAA cure >95%
HEV (RNA, Hepeviridae): fecal-oral; waterborne outbreaks; severe in pregnancy (fulminant, 20% mortality)
HEV self-limited in non-pregnant; no vaccine in India
clinicalContext: Pregnant woman in 3rd trimester with fulminant hepatitis.
nursingPriority: Consider Hepatitis E; admit to ICU, supportive care, watch for coagulopathy and encephalopathy, arrange transfer to tertiary with hepatology.

title: Brucellosis
keyPoints: Unpasteurized milk, contact with infected animals (cattle, goats)
Diagnosis: serology (Rose Bengal, standard agglutination test)
clinicalContext: Dairy farmer with recurrent undulant fever and sweats.
nursingPriority: Send blood for Brucella serology, start doxycycline + rifampicin, counsel pasteurization.

title: Anthrax
definition: Bacillus anthracis infection from infected animals/hides.
keyPoints: Forms: cutaneous (black eschar, malignant pustule), pulmonary (woolsorter — mediastinitis), GI
clinicalContext: Tannery worker with painless black eschar on forearm.
nursingPriority: Isolate, start ciprofloxacin, report to public health authority, culture swab.

title: Trachoma
definition: Chlamydia trachomatis serotypes A-C; leading cause of infectious blindness.
keyPoints: Stages: follicles → inflammation → scarring → trichiasis → corneal opacity
WHO SAFE strategy: Surgery, Antibiotic (azithromycin), Face washing, Environmental
clinicalContext: Child in endemic region with follicles on tarsal conjunctiva.
nursingPriority: Azithromycin 20 mg/kg single dose (max 1 g), face washing, environmental hygiene, notify surveillance.

title: Malaria species
keyPoints: P. vivax: benign tertian (48 h cycle), hypnozoites in liver → relapse
P. falciparum: malignant tertian; severe malaria; no hypnozoite
P. malariae: quartan (72 h); nephrotic syndrome
P. ovale: benign tertian; West Africa; hypnozoites
P. knowlesi: zoonotic from macaques; SE Asia
Treatment: ACT for Pf; CQ + primaquine x14 d for Pv/Po
clinicalContext: Traveller from Southeast Asia with P knowlesi+.
nursingPriority: Treat as Pf with ACT; severe cases IV artesunate; notify.

title: Types of prevention (primary/secondary/tertiary)
keyPoints: Primary: health promotion + specific protection (vaccines, HI education)
clinicalContext: Mammography in 50-y-old for breast cancer screening.
nursingPriority: Classify as secondary prevention (early diagnosis of asymptomatic disease).

title: Iceberg phenomenon
definition: Most disease is below the surface (subclinical/latent).
keyPoints: Important for: TB, hypertension, diabetes, HIV
clinicalContext: Community hypertension screening detects unknown cases.
nursingPriority: Apply iceberg concept — screen asymptomatic population to reveal hidden cases.

title: Maslow hierarchy of needs
clinicalContext: Post-op patient cannot breathe comfortably and has pain but also anxious about family visit.
nursingPriority: Address airway + pain (physiological) first before psychosocial/belonging needs.

title: Socio-economic indicators
keyPoints: HDI: life expectancy + education + GNI per capita
GDP, per capita income, poverty ratio
clinicalContext: India HDI rank.
nursingPriority: Cite India HDI 2022: rank 134/193, value 0.644.

title: Anthropology
definition: Study of human cultures and biology affecting health.
keyPoints: Cultural anthropology: customs, beliefs affecting health-seeking behaviour
clinicalContext: Immunization uptake low in village due to belief.
nursingPriority: Apply cultural anthropology; engage community leaders; myth-busting IEC.

title: Hardness of water
definition: Dissolved Ca and Mg salts in water.
keyPoints: Temporary hardness: bicarbonates, removed by boiling
clinicalContext: Water sample CaCO3 200 mg/L.
nursingPriority: Classify as hard; use boiling for temporary or ion-exchange for permanent hardness.

title: Theme of World Health Day
clinicalContext: Item asking 2024 WHD theme.
nursingPriority: My Health, My Right.

title: Chlorination
keyPoints: Residual chlorine 0.5 mg/L after 1 h contact = potable (free chlorine)
Breakpoint chlorination: oxidize all ammonia/organic matter before free residual
clinicalContext: After chlorinating well, residual 0.6 mg/L at 1 h.
nursingPriority: Declare safe for drinking; chlorinate weekly.

title: Air pollution indices
keyPoints: AQI India: 0-50 good, 51-100 satisfactory, 101-200 moderate, 201-300 poor, 301-400 very poor, 401-500 severe
Major pollutants: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb
clinicalContext: AQI 350 in Delhi winter.
nursingPriority: Very poor — limit outdoor activity, advise masks (N95), keep windows closed, asthma/COPD patients extra precautions.

title: No Tobacco Day
definition: WHO observance to draw attention to tobacco harms.
keyPoints: COTPA 2003 India: ban smoking in public places, advertising ban, pictorial warnings 85%
clinicalContext: Item on observance date.
nursingPriority: 31 May — WHO World No Tobacco Day.

title: Occupational hazards
clinicalContext: Sandblaster with dyspnea and eggshell calcification on CXR.
nursingPriority: Silicosis — remove from exposure, BCG vaccination, screen for TB, notify ESIC.

title: Anganwadi worker roles
keyPoints: Services: supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, growth monitoring, immunization days, health referral
clinicalContext: AWW identifies SAM child.
nursingPriority: Refer to NRC, start supplementary nutrition, engage mother, weekly weight monitoring, ensure immunization catch-up.

title: ASHA worker roles
definition: Accredited Social Health Activist — NRHM frontline worker.
keyPoints: Functions: IEC, immunization escort, JSY registration, home-based newborn care, DOTS provider, IFA distribution
HBNC: 6 visits in first 42 d after delivery
clinicalContext: ASHA home visit on day 1 postpartum.
nursingPriority: Check mother + baby, temperature, breastfeeding, lochia, danger signs; record in HBNC register.

title: CHC — population coverage
keyPoints: Services: Emergency, OPD, surgery, obstetrics, inpatient
clinicalContext: Item on population coverage.
nursingPriority: 80,000 plains, 30,000 hilly/tribal per CHC.

title: PHC — population coverage
keyPoints: Services: OPD, labor room, immunization, basic lab
clinicalContext: Item on PHC population.
nursingPriority: 30,000 plains, 20,000 hilly/tribal per PHC.

title: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY)
definition: Health insurance launched 2008 for BPL workers (superseded by PMJAY 2018).
keyPoints: RSBY coverage 30,000 INR/family; cashless at empanelled hospitals
PMJAY (Ayushman Bharat 2018): 5 lakh/family/year for 50 crore people
clinicalContext: Item on PMJAY coverage.
nursingPriority: 5 lakh INR per family per year for empanelled secondary/tertiary hospitalization.

title: MCH program
keyPoints: Components: ANC, intrapartum care, PNC, newborn care, immunization, nutrition, FP
clinicalContext: Item on MMR definition.
nursingPriority: Deaths of women from pregnancy/childbirth-related causes per 100,000 live births.

title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
definition: JSSK 2011 free entitlements for pregnant women and sick neonates.
keyPoints: Pregnant women: free delivery (including CS), drugs, diet, blood, transport
Sick newborns (<1 y): free treatment and transport
No user fees at public facilities
clinicalContext: Item on JSSK entitlements.
nursingPriority: Free delivery, drugs, diet, diagnostics, blood, transport for mother and sick newborn.
